videos.t: Modified Miller–Urey experiment based on my ideas and theories #MillerUreyExperiment
videos.desc: Instead of sparks, I use plasma that is controlled by a microcontroller. The plasma is so hot that it oxidizes the nitrogen in the trapped air inside the reaction flask. The Vigreux column serves as intermediate storage for the condensate and is supposed to give it time for chemical reactions before it runs back into the main flask. The starting substance is a mixture of distilled water and 75% formic acid, which form an azeotrope. Formic acid is used because traces of it have been detected spectroscopically in space. The aim of the modified Miller–Urey experiment is to synthesize amino acids

videos.desc:
#dobereiner #lighter #hydrogen

videos.t: Building a lab overhead stirrer from scratch
videos.desc:
#overheadstirrer

An overhead stirrer is a type of mechanical stirrer used for stirring solutions in the chemistry laboratory. However, magnetic stirrers are more commonly used for general purposes, as they are both easier to operate and maintain. Overhead stirrers, on the other hand, are better suited for stirring large quantities of solutions or thick suspensions, as well as for dissolving large quantities of solids in a solvent. Another advantage is that one is variable in the heating source. One can even use a Bunsen burner. Also, a variety of different impellers can be used.

videos.t: Making cupro, a synthetic silk
videos.desc: An easy to make artificial silk that requires only a few readily available chemicals. Cupro is also known as cuprammonium rayon. It was invented in 1890. Carbonized fibers were briefly used as filaments in light bulbs.

videos.t: Kastle-Meyer test (Presumptive blood test)
videos.desc: The Kastle–Meyer test is a presumptive blood test, in which the chemical indicator phenolphthalein is used to detect the possible presence of hemoglobin. The test was named after the American agricultural chemist, Joseph Hoeing Kastle, who in 1901, invented and tested the crude blood test, and the German physician and chemist, Erich Meyer, who modified the test in 1903.

Discover electrochemistry with a homemade Hofmann voltameter. It can be used, for example, to demonstrate the electrolytic decomposition of water. In this process, water is broken down into its two components, oxygen and hydrogen. Only off-the-shelf components and simple tools are used for construction.

videos.t: Building a replica of Faraday's generator
videos.desc:
#FaradaysGenerator #HomopolarGenerator #FaradayDisc
In 1831 Michael Faraday discovered the operating principle of electromagnetic generators. A horseshoe-shaped magnet creates a magnetic field through a disk. When the disk is turned this induces an electric current radially outward from the center toward the rim. The current flows out through the sliding spring contact, to the external circuit, and back into the center of the disk through the axle. videos.t: Building a photochromic molecular switch
videos.desc:
#molecularswitch #photochromic #laser
The photochromic molecular switch consists of a 650 nm and a 405 nm laser, two corresponding drivers, a voltage regulator, a temperature sensor, and a beam splitter. The switch is controlled by an Arduino Pro Micro. The 3D-printed holders for the lasers, the beam splitter, and the quartz cuvette are mounted directly on the customized PCB.

Edit: Photochromism in spiropyran works by breaking the C-O bond, converting the spiropyran into its color-emitting merocyanine form.

videos.desc:
#lightsaber #retractableLightsaber #retractable #laser

- Faster linear motor
- Degassing of the glycerine to remove trapped air
- Vent valve

Another option would be not to use a plunger at all, but an easily compressible gas such as CO₂. However, you would then have to dissolve CO₂ in glycerine to saturation beforehand.

By the way, the laser beam in the air is not visible to the human eye.

videos.t: Building a replica of Tesla's radio-controlled boat
videos.desc:
#nikolatesla #rcboat #drone #nRF24L01  #teslarcboot
Nikola Tesla's radio-controlled boat was the first drone ever. I reconstructed the boat using the drawings in US Patent No. 613,809. I did not replicate the original remote control, but I did design and build my own transmitter and receiver. It is based on the Arduino Nano microcontroller and the 2.4 GHz nRF24L01 transceiver module. The boat was built 1:2 scale. It is 60 cm long and weighs about 8.5 kg to get to the waterline shown in the patent drawings. Over 400 hours of work went into the project.

videos.desc:
#aquaregia #gold #nobelprize 
Aqua regia is a fuming mixture of 37% hydrochloric acid and 66% nitric acid, optimally in a molar ratio of 1:3. It can dissolve precious metals such as gold and platinum, but not all metals.

videos.desc:

The Sputnik automaton consists of an illuminated, handmade globe around which a model of the Sputnik1 satellite orbits. Like the original, the beeper circuit consists of an astable multivibrator, a Wien bridge oscillator, and an audio amplifier. For this purpose, 6 Russian germanium pnp transistors of type MP40 were used. The diode is made of the semiconductor material germanium as well and also comes from old Russian stocks. The wooden housing is designed to match the typical furniture of the time.

videos.t: Building a Geiger counter and testing different free available radioactive materials
videos.desc:
#DIY #geigercounter #radioactive
DIY α, β, and γ sensitive Geiger counter I designed and built. The highest activity was shown by an old gas mantle containing thorium dioxide, which at that time was a commonly major component of the incandescent mantle, as it is also called. All the radioactive materials can be bought with no restrictions on eBay.
I also show how to convert cpm to µSvh.

videos.t: The  Abyss, an 11kg epoxy diorama
videos.desc:
#theabyss #diorama #epoxyresin 
I'm a big fan of “The Abyss”, an American science fiction film from 1989 directed by James Cameron. Since most of the movie takes place underwater and I had an underwater diorama in mind for quite some time, the idea was born to create a diorama as a tribute to the movie. A total of 11kg of epoxy resin was poured. 22 neopixel LEDs provide the lighting for the butterfly-like alien creature, controlled by an Arduino pro micro so that all imaginable light patterns can be programmed. An HW-MS03 radar breakout serves as a motion detector. The diorama is far from perf

videos.t: Building a galvanically isolated memristor emulator
videos.desc:
#memristor #arduino # solidstaterelay
Arduino-compatible memristor emulator on a single PCB. The special feature is that the programmable memristor is galvanically isolated and bidirectional thanks to solid-state relays. The memristor has two connections and is not wired internally as a voltage divider, as is the case with digital potentiometers. The board is designed as an experimental platform. Analog inputs and I2C are broken out so that the memristor can also be controlled by other sensors or devices.

videos.desc:

I would like to get more involved with electrochemistry in the future, but these experiments are almost always associated with fiddling, wobbly electrodes, short circuits, loose contacts, and tangled cables, I came up with and built this device, which can be used universally in electrochemistry and simplifies the experimental setups.

videos.t: A novel bistable photochromic dye memristor
videos.desc:
#photochromic #memristor #CMTE
A first approach for a memristor based on a bistable photochromic dye. The photochromic substance I'm using has the catchy name cis-1,2-dicyano-1,2-bis(2,4,5-trimethyl-3-thienyl)ethene (or 1,2-bis(2,4,5-trimethyl-3-thienyl)-cis-1,2-dicyanoethene). Fortunately, there is an abbreviation: CMTE. The substance is costly (300 euros for 1 g), toxic, and difficult for private researchers to obtain. Nevertheless, I was determined to realize this idea, and I finally succeeded.​

videos.t: Building a gas chromatograph
videos.desc:
#gaschromatograph #homemade #arduino 
Gas chromatography (GC) is a separation technique using gas flow through a column that separates compounds based on both volatility and interaction with the liquid stationary phase. Professional GCs are very expensive and not affordable for schools or amateur researchers. In the video, I will show you how to build a simple CG and a column that can be used to analyze LPG or other low molecular-weight alkanes.​​
Further sources of information:
https://www.aatis.de/content/bausatz/AS656_Gaschromatograph
https://www.researchgate.net/publication/299630295_Ein_G

videos.t: Building a lab-on-a-chip
videos.desc:
#LoC #LabOnAChip #Microfluidics #SyringePump
In this video, I show you how to build a simple lab-on-a-chip and a very inexpensive, freely programmable (Arduino) syringe pump. This gives you a complete microfluidic system to carry out many experiments. For example, I have chosen a biochemical reaction based on the enzyme glucose oxidase, which can be used to detect glucose.

videos.t: Building an antimony pH meter from scratch
videos.desc:
#phmeter #diy #antimony 
In this video, I show you how to build a simple and inexpensive antimony pH meter. It is especially interesting for me because, unlike the standard glass electrode, it can be miniaturized for a lab-on-a-chip. However, the response is slower and less sensitive to low pH values. It is also susceptible to chemical corrosion. For cost reasons, I chose a copper-copper(II) sulfate electrode instead of the usual silver chloride electrode. As the cell has a low internal resistance, no BNC plug, socket, or shielded cable is required.
Further links:
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki

videos.t: Building a small, fully automatic Birkeland-Eyde experimental reactor
videos.desc:
Achtung: Die Herstellung und der Besitz von Salpetersäure über die erlaubten Konzentrationen sind für Privatpersonen in Deutschland nach der EU-Ausgangsstoffverordnung strafbar.
#Birkeland-Eyde #nitricacid 
In this video, I show you how to build a fully automatic Birkeland-Eyde reactor that you can use for further experiments or to produce nitric acid. At the moment, I am working on the theoretical basics of the Birkeland-Eyde process, which are very complex. However, it is necessary to be able to optimize. If you are interested, I will make a follow-up video.

videos.t: Making ammonia from its elements (Haber-Bosch)
videos.desc:
#hydrogen #nitrogen #ammonia #haberbosch
In this video, I show the synthesis of ammonia from its elements hydrogen and nitrogen, also known as the Haber-Bosch process. The ammonia is then detected using Berthelot's reagent. As a catalyst, I use a mixture of fine iron powder and aluminum oxide. The yield in this experiment is very low. Industrial Haber-Bosch plants work under very high pressure and with better catalysts. Please like and share the video, subscribe, and consider to become a patreon.

videos.t: The experiment that gave rise to quantum mechanics (Photoelectric effect)
videos.desc:
#photoelectriceffect #photon #quantummechanics 
In this video, I show how to build an apparatus according to Hertz/Hallwachs to demonstrate the photoelectric effect and the dependence of electron emission on the frequency of light by observing the deflection of a needle electroscope.

videos.t: Crystalloluminescence of table salt
videos.desc:
#crystalloluminescence #tablesalt #nacl #luminescence 

NaCl (table salt) is one of the few known substances in which crystalloluminescence occurs during crystallization. The crystalloluminescence can be explained by the luminescence of excited dopant cations in the crystal lattice of NaCl during the phase transformation from dissolved to solid, and not by triboluminescence of the crystals formed. videos.t: Experimental estimation of absolute zero
videos.desc:
#absolutezero #timeofflight #thermodynamics 
Experimental determination of absolute zero using a thermocouple, a ToF sensor, and a gas syringe. Data transmission via microcontroller and a cross-platform serial monitor/plotter (https://github.com/hacknus/serial-monitor-rust/releases). Evaluation in Excel using linear regression.

videos.t: Building a replica of Leeuwenhoek's single-lens microscope
videos.desc:
#Leeuwenhoek #microscope #machining
Van Leeuwenhoek's one-lens microscope design was cleverer than you might think. Watch the video to find out. Apart from a column drill, I only used basic tools like a hacksaw, files, sandpaper, hammer, and tapping sets. In addition, some parts were soft or silver soldered. The replica is made almost entirely of brass. The original was made of silver. Only the lens is modern. It is made of anti-reflective glass and has a focal length of 2 mm, which results in a magnification of around 125x. Van Leeuwenhoek's single-lens microscopes had a magnification of up t

videos.t: Experimental determination of Planck's constant using LEDs
videos.desc:
#Planck'sConstant #LED # LinearRegression
In this video, I show you how to experimentally determine the Planck constant using LEDs. I have designed a small PCB to make the measurement as convenient as possible. You can also connect an ammeter and, for example, experimentally determine the voltage-current characteristics of the LEDs. The data was analyzed in Excel. Gerber files can be found here: https://github.com/Marbslab/Planck-costant

videos.t: Bringing a Crookes tube to life
videos.desc:
#crookestube #highvoltage #fluorescent 
I bought a Crookes tube from AliExpress, which I gave a base plate and foot made of fine wood and brass feet. It took a few attempts before I got it to work—the secret is aluminum foil.

Crookes tube: https://de.aliexpress.com/item/32851034247.html
High voltage generator: https://highvoltageshop.com/10kV-HV-Generator-Modul-12VDC-1000-bis-10000VDC-Positive-High-Voltage-Generator-einstellbar

You can support me on Patreon: https://www.patreon.com/user?u=95570128

videos.t: The dawn of electrochemistry
videos.desc:
#galvani #frogGalvanoscope #animalElectricity #frankenstein 
Luigi Galvani's discovery, often called “animal electricity”, refers to his observation that a frog's muscles twitched when they came into contact with two different metals. Galvani believed these muscle twitches were caused by an electrical fluid in the body. Although he did not fully understand the exact nature of this "animal electricity", his discovery laid the foundation for the understanding of bioelectricity. It inspired Alessandro Volta to invent the first battery.

videos.t: DIY Franck-Hertz experiment
videos.desc:
#quantumphysics #FranckHertzExperiment #argon  
A DIY version of the Franck-Hertz experiment. Instead of a costly mercury tube, I use a cheap thyratron tube filled with argon. A special power supply was built for the experiment that provides an adjustable accelerating, retarding and filament voltage. The filament current can also be preset. Analog voltmeters and ammeters are integrated into the power supply. You only need a multimeter set in the µA range to measure the collector or anode current. As with the Franck-Hertz experiment, the glowing regions can also be seen, although the design of

videos.t: Powering a Geissler tube by hand
videos.desc:
#wimshurst #geissler #helium 
In this video, I show you how to operate a Geissler tube with a Wimshurst machine. The Wimshurst machine is from AliExpress, and the Geissler tube is from eBay. Geissler tubes are filled with various gases at low pressure, with metal electrodes at each end. A high voltage of several thousand volts is applied between the electrodes. The high voltage ionizes the gas, causing it to give off light by fluorescence in a glow discharge. The color of the light depends on the gas used. To give it a vintage look, I made a new base from lime wood and tube holders from turned

videos.t: Making nitric acid by the Ostwald process
videos.desc:
#nitricacid #ostwald #catalyst #drstone 
In this video, I show you the Ostwald process in an experiment. In the Ostwald process, ammonia is oxidized using a suitable catalyst to produce nitric acid. I use a catalyst that you can buy on Amazon or eBay, which is not expensive. I also show how to build a low-cost, modular lab frame for chemical experiments. Also, check out my Haber-Bosch video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=31jpvFuUQBI

videos.t: Building a programmable diaphragm pump for the lab
videos.desc:
#diaphragmpump #laboratory #arduinonano 
In this video, I show you how to build a programmable diaphragm pump for the laboratory. You can also use the pump for an aquarium. 
Microcontroller: Arduino Nano
Driver: Power MOSFET for the heating bed of a 3D printer
Diaphragm pump: 12V DC, 10 L/min max.
Interface: Rotary encoder with push-button function
Display: LCD 16 x 2, I2C
Supply voltage: 12V DC
Dimensions: 200 x 145 x 54mm

You can find the wiring diagram and the source code here: https://github.com/Marbslab/lab-pump

videos.t: DIY water chiller for the chemistry lab
videos.desc:
#waterchiller #portablefridge #chemistrylab 
Laboratory in a small space, no water connections? No problem! In the video, I show you how to build a water chiller from a portable freezer, which even allows you to precisely regulate the volume flow of the cooling water. The water chiller runs on 12V DC, so it is completely safe regarding splashing water. It is designed for smaller distillation tasks, and since it cools using a compressor, it is much more effective than cooling with Peltier elements.

videos.t: Building an immersion photometer
videos.desc:
#Photometer #Immersionphotometer #BriggsRauscher
In this video, I show you how I built an immersion photometer and used it to analyze the Briggs-Rauscher reaction.
Design files can be found here: https://github.com/Marbslab/Immersion-photometer
Cross-platform serial monitor/plotter: https://github.com/hacknus/serial-monitor-rust

videos.t: Building a rotovap
videos.desc:
#rotovap #DIY #homechemistry 
A rotary evaporator, or rotovap for short, is a piece of high-end equipment found in chemical laboratories. Since they are costly, they are usually out of reach for amateur chemists. However, a rotovap is not difficult to build. In this video, I show you how I built my own rotovap for a fraction of the price of a commercial rotovap.

Errata: It's a reflux condenser, but does not return the condensate to the system from which it originated. It just cools the vapor, which condenses and drips in the flask below the condenser. So it's not a reflux process.

videos.t: Building a voice-assisted adaptive robot hand
videos.desc:
#FRAM #gripper #speechrecognition #machinelearning #terminator 
In this video, I show how I built a voice-assisted adaptive robot hand. The adaptive gripper is a copy of the FESTO gripper from AliExpress. It is powered by a stepper motor. A photo interrupter ensures precise homing. I designed my own shield for the Arduino Uno, which, in addition to the user interface consisting of 5 push buttons and an OLED, includes a TCM 2210 silent stepper motor driver and a FRAM chip (MB85RC256V) for storing the learned objects. I also use the offline speech recognition module from DFRobot.

videos.t: Building a low-cost xenon light source for spectrometry
videos.desc:
#xenon #lightsource #opticalfiber #spectrometer 
In this video, I will show you how to build a low-cost xenon light source with an optical fiber for spectrometry. I use an H7 xenon bulb and the necessary ballast from the automotive sector. You can build the whole thing without a metal lathe or mill, but you should have some manual skills. The optical fiber is made of a special PMMA that also transmits UV light. Ordinary PMMA is suitable for wavelengths from 300 to 900 nm. The xenon light source is a sub-project of a larger project—the construction of an HPLC.

videos.t: Building an autosampler, part 1
videos.desc:
#autosampler #scararobot 
In this video, I begin building the autosampler for my HPLC project. The autosampler will be designed as a SCARA robot. The forearm is actuated by two 30 kg Waveshare bus servos with magnetic encoders, and a Nema 8 stepper motor with 5:1 planetary gearing, enabling the extendable gripper to manipulate sample vials. All aluminum parts were made by hand because I do not own a CNC mill or a metal lathe.

videos.t: Start into gel electrophoresis, part 1
videos.desc:
#electrophoresis #timer  #labpowersupply
Gel electrophoresis is a method for the separation and analysis of biomacromolecules (DNA, RNA, proteins, etc.) and their fragments, based on their size and charge through a gel. Nucleic acid molecules are separated by applying an electric field to move the negatively charged molecules through a gel matrix of agarose or other substances. Shorter molecules move faster and migrate farther than longer ones because shorter molecules migrate more easily through the pores of the gel. This phenomenon is called sieving. Proteins are separated by the charge in a

videos.t: Building a xenon flash bulb driver for my spectrometer
videos.desc:
#xenonflashbulb #flashbulbdriver #HamamatsuC12880MA 
In this video, I demonstrate a simple xenon flash bulb driver that can be controlled using any microcontroller. The triggering of the driver is completely galvanically isolated by an optocoupler. I use the xenon flash bulb as a secondary light source for my Hamamatsu C12880MA spectrometer project.

videos.t: Building a TMP117 high-accuracy temperature probe for pH measurements
videos.desc:
#TMP117 #temperature probe #arduino 
Custom circuit board with a high-accuracy TMP117 temperature sensor, encapsulated in a glass tube with non-conductive thermal paste, used for temperature compensation in pH measurements or similar applications. Suitable for Arduino, Raspberry Pi, and ESP32.

videos.t: DIY laser module
videos.desc:
#laser #laserdiodedriver #laserdiode
In the video, I present a simple n-type CW laser driver and show how I built my own laser module.

videos.t: Building a high-quality launch pad for cluster/mid power rockets
videos.desc:
#launchpad #experimentalrockets #rocketry #rockets 
This is the first part of a video series in which I will send a micro-bio lab as a payload in an amateur rocket to an altitude of about 1 km. Over time, I may also develop my own rocket motor based on eutectic or hypergolic propellants.

videos.t: N2O (nitrous oxide/laughing gas)
videos.desc:
#n2o #nitrousoxide #oxidizer #hybridrocket #laughinggas 
Just a little video about N2O (nitrous oxide/laughing gas). I wish you all a Happy New Year.

videos.t: Building an autosampler (redesign)
videos.desc:
#autosampler #TB6600 #Arduino #Steppermotor #3dprinting 
In this video, I show how I built an autosampler with a sample carousel. The autosampler can be controlled via serial or I2C or operate independently. An RTC ensures precise date and time display. The laboratory temperature is also displayed. I use an Arduino Mega as the microcontroller. The three stepper motors are controlled by TB6600s. The tray holds 30 sample bottles, each with a capacity of 20 ml. I need the autosampler for my HPLC/spectrometer project. However, the autosampler will first be used in the synthesis of Cd/Se quantum do

videos.t: Building a 3D printed rocket launch controller
videos.desc:
#rocket #launch #ematch #arduino
In this video, I show how I built a 3D printed rocket launch controller with a microcontroller (Arduino Nano Every). I also explain how a simple LiPo battery monitor works and how you can determine the capacity based on the voltage. I decided not to implement an e-match checker because the e-matches should already be checked at home with a multimeter, and I mainly fly cluster rockets, which would make things even more complicated (resistors in parallel).

videos.t: Building a portable weather station for rocketry
videos.desc:
#anemometer #BME280 #arduino #weatherstation 
3D-printed weather station that can be mounted on a camera tripod, featuring a Bosch BME280, an ultrasonic anemometer, a battery monitor, and a 2" TFT display. An onboard compass allows the anemometer to be aligned northward, displaying the correct wind direction in addition to wind speed.

videos.t: I built a single board analog computer (open source)
videos.desc:
#analogcomputer #opamp #oscilloscope #opensource 
In this video, I show my homemade analog single-board computer. I built it to learn and explore neuromorphic circuits so I can hopefully build a neuromorphic computer one day. The project is open source, the files can be found here: https://github.com/Marbslab/Analog-computer
The analog computer features two adders, two multipliers, two integrators, two multi-purpose opamps, and function generators (square, triangle, and sine). The 3D-printed housing has a modular design. I was inspired by the AKAT-1 analog computer from the 1950s. As with the

videos.t: Towards a neuromorphic & wetware computer
videos.desc:
#neuromorphic  #wetware #memristor #pong #microfluidics 
Sponsor of this video: https://www.pcbway.com/ 
PCBs, PCB assembly, 3D printing, CNC machining, metal sheet fabrication, and injection molding — super-fast, high-quality, and very affordable. Everything you need for your next project.

In this video, I’ll give you an overview of my neuromorphic/wetware computer project. I’m also working on a chemical neuron as a microfluidic device.

Idea for the electrode array: https://forum.hackteria.org/t/diy-neuron-chip-instruction/694/4
Wetware computer that uses human neurons: https://corticallabs

videos.t: Building a terrestrial rover to explore the ecosystem, part 1
videos.desc:
#Rover #rockerbogie #4WD
In this video series, I’m building a terrestrial rover designed to explore the ecosystem. It’s equipped with 4WD and a rocker-bogie suspension system. The camera pan-tilt unit uses bus servos with magnetic encoders. The wheels are from Servo City and have a diameter of 140 mm. Currently, the rover is controlled via a PS2 gamepad (Bluetooth). The frame is made of inexpensive 2020 aluminum extrusions. Other components are laser-cut or 3D-printed. I designed most of the PCBs myself. The rover is powered by a 3S LiPo battery with a capacity of 7.5 Ah. In the next part of t

videos.t: Desktop demonstration of the Fischer-Tropsch synthesis
videos.desc:
#fischertropsch #snygas #gasoline
Since I am particularly interested in large-scale chemical processes, I decided to tackle the Fischer-Tropsch synthesis this time. The Fischer–Tropsch process is a series of chemical reactions that converts a mixture of carbon monoxide and hydrogen, known as syngas, into liquid hydrocarbons. These reactions occur in the presence of metal catalysts, typically at temperatures of 150–300 °C. In total, I spent 200 hours working on this project—one of the most nerve-wracking undertakings.

videos.t: Cracking paraffin oil on your desk
videos.desc:
#cracking #homelab #bromine  #electrolysis  
In this video, I demonstrate how cracking paraffin oil yields flammable gases and liquids. I use bromine water—which I produced in a homemade electrolysis cell—as evidence of the presence of alkenes. Spoiler: the heating jacket had a major malfunction. Fortunately, though, it didn’t happen until after the experiment.

videos.t: Building an organic flow battery based on green tea
videos.desc:
#Flowbattery #Matcha #egcg 
In this video, we explore organic flow batteries and build one using green tea (matcha). Here, the compound epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG) serves as the electrolyte in an alkaline environment. It’s called a “flow” battery because the electrolyte is moved through a stir bar. In addition to EGCG, gallic acid and pyrogallol can also be used as electrolytes.
Link to the research paper: https://www.pedocs.de/frontdoor.php?source_opus=17393

videos.t: Building a micro distill
videos.desc:
#microdistill #temperaturecontroller #microchemistry #homelab 
Since the amounts of substances in chemistry are getting smaller and smaller (microscale chemistry, microfluidics, etc.), I’m attempting to build a microdistiller this time. Of course, this also requires a laboratory heating mantle. Since you can’t buy one for a tiny 25-ml round-bottom flask, I made it myself out of scrap aluminum. The heating mantle could be improved even further if I had a metal lathe.

videos.t: Building a Hamamatsu phototube flame scanner
videos.desc:
#UVTRON #Flamesensor #hamamatsu #R2868 #wildfire
A 3D-printed 360° flame scanner based on the Hamamatsu UVTRON R2868 phototube. I designed it for my terrestrial rover to detect wildfires early on. A slip ring and a bus servo with a magnetic encoder ensure smooth movements. The YouTube channel Project 326 has also created a great video about the R2868 phototube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yh_ctoDg_v4

videos.t: Building a mini chemistry lab
videos.desc:
#chemistryexperiments #homelab  #woodworking  #liebigcondenser
I designed this mini chemistry lab for beginners and for those who have very little space. Traditional chemistry sets are often bulky, intimidating, and require a lot of storage. You will also learn how to make your own electric test-tube heater and a tiny Liebig condenser from simple materials.
Useful links:
